passages.title: Stop Wasting Food
text: Walk past the back of almost any restaurant or wedding reception at the end of the night and you will see bins full of rice, meat, and vegetables that nobody ate. Food waste has become one of our most serious and least discussed problems. It is time for every household, business, and school to take action against it.

The scale of the problem is enormous. A study by Indonesia's national development planning agency, Bappenas, estimated that between 2000 and 2019 the country wasted around 115 to 184 kilograms of food per person every year. That is food that could have fed millions of people, while many families still struggle to afford healthy meals.

Wasted food also wastes everything that went into producing it: land, water, fertilizer, fuel, and human labour. Furthermore, when food rots in landfills, it produces methane, a greenhouse gas many times more powerful than carbon dioxide over a short period. Reducing food waste is therefore one of the simplest ways to fight climate change.

Much of this waste happens at the very end of the chain, in our own homes and at events. We cook too much, buy more than we need because of discounts, and throw away food that is still perfectly safe to eat simply because it does not look perfect.

We can all do better. Households should plan meals, write shopping lists, and store leftovers properly. Restaurants and caterers should offer smaller portions and donate surplus food to food banks. Schools should teach students to take only what they will eat. And the government should make it easier for businesses to donate food safely. If we all act now, we can turn waste into meals and protect our planet at the same time.

passages.title: Think Before You Click
text: "Congratulations! You have won a new phone. Click this link to claim your prize." Messages like this arrive on millions of phones every day, and every day some people believe them. Online scams are becoming more common and more convincing, and everyone, especially young people, must learn to protect themselves.

Scammers are no longer easy to recognize. Many of them use the names and logos of real banks, delivery companies, or government offices. Some send files that look like wedding invitations or delivery receipts but actually install programs that steal banking information. Others pretend to be friends or relatives who urgently need money.

Young people are not safe simply because they are good with technology. In fact, their confidence can make them careless. They tend to share more personal information online, shop on unfamiliar websites, and respond quickly to messages without checking them. Scammers know this and design traps that target them, such as fake job offers, investment schemes promising quick profits, and offers of free game credits.

The consequences can be serious. Victims may lose their savings, have their accounts taken over, or find loans taken out in their names. Beyond the financial damage, many victims feel ashamed and do not report the crime, which allows scammers to continue.

We must therefore develop a habit of thinking before we click. Never open files or links from unknown senders. Check the official website or call the company's official number before responding to any message about prizes, payments, or account problems. Never share one-time passwords (OTP) with anyone. And if you are tricked, report it immediately to your bank and the police. Schools and parents should talk openly about online scams, so that no one is too embarrassed to ask for help.

passages.title: Let's Use AI Tools Wisely at School
text: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools that can write essays, solve maths problems, and summarize books in seconds are now available to any student with a phone. Some schools have responded by banning them completely. This is the wrong approach. Instead, schools should teach students to use AI tools wisely and honestly.

First, banning AI is almost impossible to enforce. Students can access these tools at home or on their own devices, and it is difficult to prove that a piece of writing was produced by AI. A ban would simply push their use out of sight, where teachers cannot guide it.

Second, AI tools can genuinely support learning when used properly. A student who is confused about a topic can ask an AI tool to explain it in simpler words or give more examples. A writer can use it to get feedback on the organization of an essay. Used in this way, AI acts like a patient tutor that is available at any time.

However, AI tools also have real limitations. They sometimes produce information that sounds convincing but is completely wrong, and they may invent sources that do not exist. Students who copy answers without checking them may learn nothing and may even spread false information. This is precisely why students need guidance.

Schools should therefore create clear rules on when and how AI may be used, and they should require students to state when they have used it. Teachers should design assignments that require personal reflection and classroom discussion. Most importantly, students must remember that AI should help them think, not think for them.

questions.question: What does the writer want readers to do?

options.B: Visit landfills to see the problem
options.D: Take action to reduce food waste

questions.explanation: Tesis hortatori: It is time for every household, business, and school to take action against it.

questions.question: Why does the writer mention methane?

options.A: To explain why food rots quickly
options.B: To compare different types of fertilizer
options.C: To show that food waste contributes to climate change
options.D: To describe how landfills are built

questions.explanation: Makanan yang membusuk menghasilkan metana, gas rumah kaca yang kuat, sehingga mengurangi sampah makanan membantu melawan perubahan iklim.

questions.question: What is the function of the last paragraph?

options.A: To present a new argument about food banks
options.B: To describe the problem in restaurants
options.C: To repeat the statistics from paragraph 2
options.D: To give recommendations to different groups

questions.explanation: Ciri khas hortatory exposition: bagian recommendation berisi saran untuk rumah tangga, restoran, sekolah, dan pemerintah.

questions.question: Which statement is supported by the information in paragraph 2?

options.A: The estimate comes from a government agency study.
options.B: Every Indonesian throws away exactly 184 kg of food per year.
options.C: Food waste has increased every year since 2000.
options.D: Most food waste comes from restaurants.

questions.explanation: Data berasal dari kajian Bappenas. Angkanya berupa rentang perkiraan (115–184 kg), bukan angka pasti, dan teks tidak menyebut tren tiap tahun atau sumber terbesar.

questions.question:
Which uses of AI would the writer consider wise?
(1) Asking for a simpler explanation of a difficult topic
(2) Copying an AI essay and submitting it as one's own work
(3) Getting feedback on how an essay is organized
(4) Using AI sources without checking whether they exist
questions.explanation: Paragraf 3 menyebut meminta penjelasan lebih sederhana dan umpan balik susunan esai sebagai cara yang tepat. Menyalin tanpa menyatakan dan memakai sumber tanpa memeriksa justru diperingatkan di paragraf 4–5.

questions.question: The sentence AI should help them think, not think for them means that students should ....

options.B: use AI to support their own thinking rather than replace it
options.C: let AI make decisions for them

questions.explanation: Kalimat penutup menegaskan AI sebagai alat bantu berpikir, bukan pengganti proses berpikir siswa.
